item.title: €450,000 announced for Clontoe Road
item.description: A funding allocation of €450,000 has been announced for resurfacing works on the Clontoe Road from Ballinode to Scotstown. The funding was revealed at yesterday's sitting of Monaghan County Council by Chief Executive Robert Burns. It will offer a safe and alternative road for everyone to use to access Scotstown, Ballinode and Kilmore football field. item.description: A local councillor says it's an "absolute disgrace" that a road has been closed in the Newbliss area for almost eight months. item.title: Monaghan remain bottom of Division 1 league table
item.description: Monaghan fell further into relegation trouble after a 14-point loss to Kerry in Killarney. The result means Monaghan are bottom of division One with no points and just two games remaining. The Farney side had trailed by just one at half-time and manager Gabriel Bannigan admitted Kerry punished mistakes. item.title: Drug driving on the rise across Monaghan says local garda
item.description: Drug driving is on the increase across Co Monaghan roads according to local Gardai. Garda Samantha Brown who is attached to Monaghan Roads Policing unit says she is encountering drug driving at all times of the day and night. Garda Brown says driving under the influence of illicit drugs not only puts the driver at risk but also passengers and others who share the road. item.title: End of IFA protest a welcome development says local councillor
item.description: A local councillor has welcomed the end of the IFA protest at Bord Bia HQ. Cllr Pauric Clerkin says after over 28 days it's welcome news that the commitment of the independent governance review has been given. He says the commitment to a full and transparent review is an important step toward restoring confidence and ensuring robust governance structures within Bord Bia. item.title: Co Cavan dog wins coveted national title
item.description: A Co Cavan dog has won a coveted national title. After receiving hundreds of truly heartwarming nominations from across the country, the Irish Kennel Club have announce the seven category winners for the Golden Paw Hero Dog Awards 2026. The awards aim to find and reward Ireland's most courageous, brave and life changing canines in order to honour the love, companionship and service they give us on a day-to-day basis.
